newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end sharply higher across the board.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end sharply higher across the board.

text.p: Anticipation of lower interest rates sparked broad-based buying and sent the Seoul stock market sharply higher on Monday, brokers said.
The composite stock index rose 18.02 points or 2.32 percent to provisionally close at 795.33. Gainers beat losers 700 to 216 with 259 stocks going limit up.
President Kim Young-sam will head an economic ministers' meeting on Wedensday, and many investors believed the government will unveil a cut in banks' reserve requirments at the meeting.
But government officials said they could not confirm the market speculation at this stage.

"Although it's not officially confirmed, many investors hope the government will cut the rate one way or another," said Hwang Chang-joong, analyst at LG Securities, referring to President Kim's comments that South Korea needs some measures to cure its economic problems of high cost and low efficiency.
Casey Chae, analyst at Union Bank of Switzerland said: "Interest rate sensitve shares like low-priced large-cap shares came under the spotlight today."
Daewoo Group shares climbed on active institutional bargain hunting following a positive market re-evaluation of the group's globalisation policy, brokers said.
Both Daewoo Heavy Industries and Daewoo Electronics went limit up, gaining 390 won and 380 won each to 6,960 and 6,840 respectively.
Strong buying interest in Samsung Electronics spread to other core blue chips. Samsung Electronics added 3,700 won to 69,700 and POSCO gained 400 won to 42,800.
Brokers said North Korea's threat to retaliate over a submarine incident was unlikely to have any further impact on the market.
Hwang said the market would show steady rises up to the 810 level. -- YEOM YOON-JEONG (822) 727 5647
